'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak was asked about a man who says: "Humayd al-Tawil (the tall), Sulayman al-A'mash (the weak-eyed), Humayd al-A'raj (the lame), Marwan al-Asghar (the younger)," and he said: "If you intend to describe him and do not intend to insult him, there is no harm in it."

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sarjis, who said: "I saw al-Asla'" (the bald one), meaning 'Umar, kissing the Black Stone. In another narration: al-Usayla'.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does not repent﴾, that is, from these nicknames by which the listeners are hurt. ﴿Then those are the wrongdoers﴾, because they wrong themselves by committing these prohibited acts.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 49, verse 12 (part 1 of 3)**

There are ten issues in this verse.

**The first issue:** the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, avoid much suspicion﴾. It was said that this verse was revealed concerning two men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who backbit a companion of theirs. The reason was that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he travelled, would pair a needy man with two well-off men, who would serve them. He paired Salman with two men. Salman went ahead to the lodging, but sleep overcame him and he fell asleep without preparing anything for them. When they arrived, they found no food or condiment. They said to him: "Go and ask the Prophet (ﷺ) for food and condiment for us." He went, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript K.]] "Go to Usamah ibn Zayd and say to him: if you have any surplus of food, let him give it to you." Usamah was the treasurer of the Prophet (ﷺ). Salman went to him, and Usamah said: "I have nothing." He returned to them and informed them. They said: "He did have it, but he was stingy." Then they sent Salman to a group of the Companions, but he found nothing with them. They said: "If we had sent Salman to the Well of Sumayhah [[An ancient well in Medina with abundant water.]], its water would have dried up." Then the two of them set out spying to see whether Usamah had anything. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw them and said: "What is this? I see the green of meat in your mouths." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, we have not eaten meat or anything else today." He said: "Rather, you have been eating the flesh of Salman and Usamah." Then the verse was revealed: "O you who believe, avoid much suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin." This was related by al-Tha'labi. That is: do not think ill of the people of goodness if you know from their outward conduct that they are good.

**The second issue:** it is established in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy, do not seek out secrets, do not outbid one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn away from one another, and be, O servants of Allah, brothers." This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Our scholars said: suspicion here and in the verse means accusation (tuhmah). The prohibition and warning apply only to an accusation for which there is no cause that makes it necessary, such as one who is accused of indecency or of drinking wine, when nothing has appeared from him that would call for it. The evidence that suspicion here means accusation is the words "and do not spy", because a person may first have a passing thought of accusation and then want to investigate, search for it, look and listen to confirm what has come to him of that accusation. So the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade that. If you wish, you may say: what distinguishes the suspicions that must be avoided from others is that every suspicion for which no sound indication and apparent cause is known is forbidden and must be avoided.

This applies when the person thought of is one who has been seen to be upright and righteous, and who is known outwardly for trustworthiness. Then to suspect him of corruption or treachery is forbidden. This is unlike one whom people know to be given to doubtful conduct and open to vile acts. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has made it unlawful to harm a Muslim's blood and honour, and to think ill of him." It is related from al-Hasan: "We lived in a time when thinking well of people was obligatory. You live today in a time when it is said: act, keep silent, and think of people whatever you wish."

**The third issue:** suspicion has two states. One is a state that becomes known and strengthened through some kind of evidence, and judgment may be given on its basis. Most rulings of the Sharia are built on preponderant assumption (ghalabat al-zann), such as analogy (qiyas), the report of a single narrator (khabar al-wahid), and other things, like the assessment of destroyed property and the compensation for injuries. The second state is when something occurs in the soul without any indication, so that it is no more likely than its opposite. This is doubt (shakk), and it is not permissible to judge by it. This is what is forbidden, as we have established just above.

A group of innovators denied that Allah is worshipped through suspicion and that acting upon it is permissible, claiming this as an arbitrary ruling in religion and an assertion against reason. There is no sound basis for this to rely upon, for the Creator, the Exalted, did not condemn all of it; He only mentioned condemnation of some of it. Some of them have clung to the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "Beware of suspicion." But there is no proof in this, because suspicion in the Sharia is of two kinds: praiseworthy and blameworthy. The praiseworthy is that by which the religion of the one who suspects and of the one suspected remains sound when it is put to the test. The blameworthy is its opposite, as shown by His words: "Indeed, some suspicion is sin," and His words: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of one another and say, "This is an obvious lie"?﴾ [24:12], and His words: ﴿And you thought an evil thought and became a ruined people﴾ [48:12]. The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "If one of you is praising his brother, let him say: I think he is such, and I do not vouch for anyone before Allah." And he said: "If you suspect, do not be certain; if you envy, do not transgress; and if you feel ill omen, go ahead." This was recorded by Abu Dawud.

Most scholars hold that a bad opinion of one whose outward conduct is good is not permissible, and that there is no fault in a bad opinion of one whose outward conduct is bad. This was said by al-Mahdawi.

**The fourth issue:** the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And do not spy﴾. Abu Raja' and al-Hasan, with variation, and others recited it as "and do not tahassassu" with a ḥā' (ح). Scholars differed as to whether the two words have one meaning or two. Al-Akhfash said: the one is not far from the other, because tajassus is searching for what is hidden from you, while tahassus, with the ḥā', is seeking news and searching for it. It was also said that tajassus, with the jīm (ج), is searching, and from it comes the phrase "a man who is a spy (jasus)" when he searches into affairs. With the ḥā', it refers to what a person perceives through some of his senses. A second opinion on the distinction is that with the ḥā' it means seeking it for oneself, while with the jīm it means acting as an agent for someone else. This was said by Tha'lab. The first is better known. One says: "I searched out (jassastu) the news and I investigated it (tajassastuhā)," meaning I examined it thoroughly, and from this comes the word "spy" (jasus).

The meaning of the verse is: take what appears, and do not pursue the faults of the Muslims. That is, none of you should search for the defect of his brother until he finds it out after Allah has covered it. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Mu'awiyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If you pursue the faults of people, you will corrupt them, or you will nearly corrupt them." Abu al-Darda' said: this is a word which Mu'awiyah heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and by it Allah benefited him.

It is related on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If the ruler seeks out doubt among the people, he corrupts them." It is related on the authority of Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Mas'ud was brought word that a certain man's beard was dripping with wine. Abdullah said: "We have indeed been forbidden to spy, but if something appears to us, we will act upon it."

It is related on the authority of Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of those who have believed with their tongues while faith has not entered their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues the faults of others, Allah will pursue his fault, and whoever Allah pursues his fault, He will expose him within his own house."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: One night I kept watch with Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) in Medina, when a lamp appeared to us in a house whose door was ajar, belonging to a people who had raised voices and noisy chatter. Umar said: "This is the house of Rabi'ah ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and they are now drinking. What do you think?" I said: "I think we have come to what Allah has forbidden." He said: Allah the Exalted says: "And do not spy," and we have spied. So Umar turned away and left them.

Abu Qilabah said: Umar ibn al-Khattab was told that Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi was drinking wine with some companions in his house. Umar went until he entered upon him, and there was no one with him except one man. Abu Mihjan said: "This is not lawful for you! Allah has forbidden you from spying." So Umar went out and left him.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: Umar and Abd al-Rahman went out patrolling at night, when a fire appeared to them. They asked permission to enter, and the door was opened. There was a man and a woman singing, and the man had a cup in his hand. Umar said: "And you with this, so-and-so?" He said: "And you with this, Commander of the Faithful!" Umar said: "Who is this woman to you?" He said: "My wife." Umar said: "What is in this cup?" He said: "Pure water." Then he said to the woman: "And what is it that you are singing?" She said:

*The night has grown long and its sides have darkened,*
*And sleeplessness troubles me that I have no beloved to play with.*
*By Allah, were it not for Allah, whom I watch over,*
*This couch would have been shaken from its sides.*
*But my reason and my modesty restrain me,*
*And I honour my husband so that his mounts are not reached.*

Then the man said: "This is not what we were commanded, O Commander of the Faithful!" Allah the Exalted says: "And do not spy" (49:12). He said: "You are right." I say: it cannot be understood from this report that the woman was other than the man's wife, because 'Umar would not approve of fornication; rather, she sang those verses in remembrance of her husband, and she said them during his absence from her [see this story in vol. 3, p. 108 of this book]. And Allah knows best.

'Amr ibn Dinar said: A man from the people of Madinah had a sister who fell ill, and he would visit her, until she died, and he buried her. He was the one who went down into her grave, and a pouch containing dinars fell from his sleeve. He sought help from some of her family, and they dug up her grave, and he took the pouch. Then he said: "I will uncover her until I see what has become of my sister." So he uncovered her, and behold, the grave was blazing with fire. He came to his mother and said: "Tell me, what was the deed of my sister?" She said: "Your sister has died, so what is your question about her deeds!" He kept pressing her until she said: "Among her deeds was that she delayed the prayer beyond its times, and whenever the neighbours slept, she would go to their houses and put her ear to their doors, eavesdropping on them and disclosing their secrets." He said: "By this she was destroyed!"

Fifth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not some of you backbite others﴾. He, mighty and majestic, forbade backbiting (ghibah), which is mentioning a man with what is in him. If you mention him with what is not in him, it is slander (buhtan). Its meaning is established in Sahih Muslim from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "What do you think if what I say is true of my brother?" He said: "If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him, and if it is not in him, you have slandered him."

It is said: "ightaba-hu igtiyaban" when one falls into it, and the noun is ghibah, which is mentioning a fault in someone's absence. [Al-zahr: what is absent from you.]

Al-Hasan said: Backbiting has three aspects, all of which are in the Book of Allah: ghibah, ifk and buhtan. As for ghibah, it is that you say about your brother what is in him. As for ifk, it is that you say about him what has reached you about him. As for buhtan, it is that you say about him what is not in him.

It is narrated from Shu'bah that he said: Mu'awiyah (i.e. Ibn Qurrah) said to me: "If a man who is one-handed passes by you and you say, 'This one-handed man,' that would be backbiting." Shu'bah said: I mentioned this to Abu Ishaq, and he said: "He is right."

Abu Hurairah reported that a man of Aslam came to the Prophet ﷺ and testified against himself to having committed fornication, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned him. The Prophet ﷺ heard two of his companions saying, one to the other: "Look at this man whom Allah concealed, yet his own soul did not leave him alone until he was stoned like a dog." He remained silent about them. Then he walked for a while until he passed a carcass of a donkey with its leg raised, and he said: "Where are so-and-so and so-and-so?" They said: "Here we are, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Dismount and eat from the carcass of this donkey." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, who would eat from this?" He said: "What you two have taken from the honour of your brother is worse than eating from it. By Him in whose hand my soul is, he is now in the rivers of Paradise, immersing himself in them."

Sixth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾. Allah likened backbiting to eating carrion, because the dead person does not know that his flesh is being eaten, just as the living person does not know of the backbiting done against him. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah only struck this parable for backbiting because eating the flesh of the dead is forbidden and loathsome, and likewise backbiting is forbidden in religion and ugly in souls. Qatadah said: Just as one of you refuses to eat the flesh of his brother when he is dead, so he must refrain from backbiting him while he is alive. The eating of flesh was used in place of backbiting because this is the custom of the Arabs. A poet said:

If they eat my flesh, I have kept their flesh intact;
And if they demolish my glory, I have built glory for them.

[The verse is by al-Muqanna' al-Kindi, whose name is Muhammad ibn 'Umairah.]

The Prophet ﷺ said: "He who continues to eat the flesh of people does not fast." So he likened disparaging people to eating their flesh. Whoever belittles a Muslim or tears his honour is like one who eats his flesh while he is alive, and whoever backbites him is like one who eats his flesh when he is dead.

In the book of Abu Dawud, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When I was taken up on the night journey, I passed by a people who had nails of copper, scratching their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are those who eat the flesh of people and violate their honour.'"

From al-Mustawrid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever eats a morsel at the expense of a Muslim man, Allah will feed him the like of it from Jahannam; and whoever is clothed with a garment at the expense of a Muslim man, Allah will clothe him with the like of it from Jahannam; and whoever stands in for a man in a position of showing off and display, Allah will stand him in the position of showing off and display on the Day of Resurrection."

His saying ﷺ has already been mentioned earlier: "O assembly of those who have believed with their tongues while faith has not entered their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims." And his saying to the two men: "What is this I see, the greenness of meat in your mouths?"

Abu Qilabah al-Raqashi said: I heard Abu 'Asim say: "I have not backbitten anyone since I learned what backbiting entails." Maymun ibn Siyah would not backbite anyone, and he would not let anyone backbite another in his presence; he would forbid it, and if the person desisted, well and good, otherwise he would stand up.

Al-Tha'labi mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: A man rose from the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and they noticed a weakness in his standing, so they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how weak so-and-so is!" He said: "You have eaten the flesh of your brother and backbitten him."

From Sufyan al-Thawri, who said: The least of backbiting is that you say, "So-and-so is curly-haired and kinky-haired," except that this is disliked. [Al-ja'd in describing men can be praise or blame: praise means strong in strength and character, or curly-haired, the opposite of straight-haired. Blame means short and of mixed character. It may also be applied to the miser; one says: a man jaʿd al-yadayn. Al-qatt: short and curly of hair.]

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Beware of mentioning people, for it is a disease, and upon you is the remembrance of Allah, for it is a cure."

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, heard a man backbiting another, and said: "Beware of backbiting, for it is the condiment of the dogs of people."

It was said to ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd: "So-and-so has fallen into you until we pitied you." He said: "Then pity him."

A man said to al-Hasan: "I have heard that you backbite me!" He said: "Your standing with me has not reached the point that I would make you judge over my good deeds."

Seventh: Some people held that backbiting occurs only in religion and does not occur in physical form or lineage. They said: "That is the act of Allah concerning him." Others held the opposite, saying: "Backbiting occurs only in physical form, character, and lineage. Backbiting in physical form is more severe, for whoever criticizes a craft has criticized its craftsman." All of this is rejected. As for the first view, it is refuted by the hadith of ʿAisha when she said about Safiyyah: "She is a short woman." The Prophet ﷺ said to her: "You have said a word which, if it were mixed into the sea, would mix it." Abu Dawud related it. At-Tirmidhi said of it: "A hasan sahih hadith." Whatever is similar in meaning is as already mentioned. And there is the consensus of the scholars of old that this is backbiting when the intention is to disparage. As for the second view, it too is rejected by all the scholars, because from the earliest times, the scholars among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Successors after them did not regard backbiting as anything more grave than backbiting concerning religion, since the disparagement of religion is the greatest of disparagements; every believer dislikes being mentioned in his religion more than he dislikes being mentioned in his body. And sufficient as a refutation of whoever holds this view is his peace be upon him saying: "If you say about your brother what he dislikes, you have backbitten him..." [the hadith]. Whoever claims that this is not backbiting has contradicted explicitly what the Prophet ﷺ said. And sufficient is the general wording of the Prophet ﷺ: "Your blood, your property, and your honour are forbidden to you," which is general to religion and worldly life. And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever has an injustice against his brother concerning his honour or his property, let him seek his pardon for it." He made it cover every honour, so whoever particularises some of this over others has opposed what the Prophet ﷺ said.

Eighth: There is no disagreement that backbiting is one of the major sins, and that whoever backbites someone must repent to Allah, mighty and majestic. Is it required that the backbiter seek the other's forgiveness? This has been disputed. One group said: he is not required to seek his forgiveness; it is only a sin between him and his Lord. They argued that he has taken nothing of his property, nor has he harmed his body in a way that diminishes it, so it is not an injustice for which he must seek pardon; an injustice is only that for which there is compensation or recompense in property or body. Another group said: it is an injustice, and its expiation is to ask Allah's forgiveness for the person he backbit. They relied on a report narrated from al-Hasan who said: "The expiation of backbiting is that you ask forgiveness for the one you backbit." Another group said: it is an injustice, and it is obligatory to seek his pardon for it. They relied on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever has an injustice against his brother concerning his honour or property, let him seek his pardon for it before a day comes when there will be no dinar or dirham, and if he has good deeds, some will be taken from them according to his injustice, and if he has no good deeds, some of the sins of his companion will be taken and added to his sins." Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has an injustice against his brother concerning his honour or anything else, let him seek his pardon today, before there is no dinar nor dirham. If he has good deeds, some will be taken from him in proportion to his injustice, and if he has no good deeds, some of the sins of his companion will be taken and placed upon him."

This meaning has already been discussed in the sura of Al ʿImran at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive﴾ [Al ʿImran: 169]. It has been narrated from the hadith of ʿAisha that a woman entered upon her, and when she rose, another woman said: "How long her train is!" ʿAisha said to her: "You have backbitten her, so seek her pardon." Thus the reports from the Prophet ﷺ indicate that it is an injustice which the backbiter must seek to be pardoned for. As for the statement of one who says: "Backbiting is only concerning property and body," the scholars have agreed that the slanderer owes the slandered an injustice for which he is punished by the prescribed penalty until he establishes it against him, and that is neither in the body nor in property. In this there is evidence that injustice occurs in honour, body and property. Allah the Exalted said concerning the slanderer: ﴿Then, since they did not bring witnesses, it is they who are liars in the sight of Allah﴾ [An-Nur: 13]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever slanders a believer with what is not in him, Allah will confine him in the clay of khabal." [Khabal: corruption, which occurs in deeds, bodies and minds. "Tinat al-khabal": the residue of the people of the Fire.] All of that is in other than property and body. As for him who says: "It is an injustice, and its expiation is to ask forgiveness for its owner," he has contradicted himself, for having named it an injustice, then said its expiation is to ask forgiveness for its owner. For his saying "injustice" establishes the wronged party's grievance, and once the grievance is established, it is removed from the wrongdoer only by the wronged party's pardon. As for the saying of al-Hasan, it is not a proof. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever has an injustice against his brother concerning honour or property, let him seek his pardon for it." Some scholars went to the view of abandoning seeking pardon for one who asks for it, and held that he does not pardon...

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib was among those who did not permit what Allah had forbidden. He said: "I will not absolve someone who wronged me."

It was said to Ibn Sirin: "O Abu Bakr, this man asks you to absolve him of an injustice he committed against you." He replied: "I did not forbid it to him so that I could permit it. Allah forbade backbiting (ghiba) to him, and I would never permit what Allah has forbidden."

The Prophet's ﷺ report indicates absolution, and it is the proof and the clarifier. Absolution indicates forgiveness, and in one sense it is pardon. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:40].

Ninth: Excluded from this category is the backbiting of the open sinner who proclaims his sin and flaunts it, for in the report: "Whoever throws off the cloak of modesty has no backbiting against him." The Prophet ﷺ also said: "Mention the wicked person for what he has done, so that people may beware of him." Backbiting, then, applies to the person who conceals himself.

It is narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "Three people have no sanctity: the follower of desires, the open sinner, and the oppressive ruler." When al-Hajjaj died, al-Hasan said: "O Allah, You caused him to die, so cut off from us his sunna" (and in another narration, "his shame"). "He came to us as a small, shrunken man, stretching out a hand with short fingers. By Allah, no dust ever settled on him in the way of Allah. He combed his hair and strutted in his gait. He climbed the pulpit and thundered until he missed the prayer. He feared neither Allah nor shame before people. Allah is above him, and beneath him are a hundred thousand or more, and none says to him, 'Prayer, O man!'" Then al-Hasan said: "Far-fetched! The sword and the whip prevented that."

Al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "The people of innovation have no backbiting."

Likewise, when you say to a judge, seeking his help in taking your right from one who wronged you: "So-and-so wronged me, or angered me, or betrayed me, or struck me, or slandered me, or mistreated me," this is not backbiting. The scholars of the Ummah are unanimous on this. The Prophet ﷺ said concerning this: "The one with a right has the right to speak." He also said: "Delaying payment by the wealthy is injustice," and: "The procrastination of one who is able (al-wajid, the one capable of paying his debt) makes his honour and his punishment lawful."

Among this category is seeking a fatwa (al-istifta'), as when Hind said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Abu Sufyan is a stingy man who does not give me what suffices me and my son. May I take from his property without his knowledge?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes, take it." She described him with stinginess and with wronging her and her son, and he did not consider her a backbiter, because he had not reproached her; rather, he answered her with a legal ruling (fatwa), upon him be prayers and peace.

Similarly, if there is a benefit in mentioning someone negatively, as when the Prophet ﷺ said: "As for Mu'awiya, he is a poor man with no wealth; and as for Abu Jahm, he does not put down his staff from his shoulder." [Abu Jahm is Ibn Hudhayfa ibn Ghanim al-Qurashi. His saying "he does not put down his staff" means that he beats women. It was also said it is a metaphor for his frequent travels, since a traveller carries his staff on journeys.] This is permissible, and his intention was that Fatima bint Qays should not be deceived by them. [Fatima was the sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays. She was one of the early emigrants, possessed beauty, intellect and perfection. She had been married to Abu 'Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughira, who divorced her. Then Mu'awiya and Abu Jahm proposed to her, and she consulted the Prophet ﷺ about them. He advised her to marry Usama ibn Zayd, and she did.]

Al-Muhasibi, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned all of this.

Tenth: The words of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿dead﴾ (maytan), and it is read as ﴿mayyitan﴾ (mayyitan). It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (al-hal) of the flesh. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative as an object of ﴿akh﴾ (brother). When He, mighty and majestic, made them acknowledge that none of them would wish to eat the carcass of his brother, He followed that with His words, exalted is He: ﴿so you would dislike it﴾ (fa-karihtumuhu). There are two interpretations: First, "you dislike eating carrion, so likewise dislike backbiting." This meaning was transmitted from Mujahid. Second, "you dislike that people backbite you, so dislike the backbiting of people." Al-Farra' said: "That is, you have already disliked it, so do not do it." It was also said: the wording is a report but its meaning is a command, that is, "dislike it." ﴿Fear Allah﴾ is coordinated with it. It was also said it is coordinated with His words: ﴿avoid much suspicion﴾ and ﴿do not spy﴾. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 49, verse 13 (part 1 of 2):

There are seven issues concerning it.

The first: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, We have created you from a male and a female﴾. That is, Adam and Hawwa' (Eve). The verse was revealed concerning Abu Hind. Abu Dawud mentioned it in (al-Marasil), [saying]: "Amr ibn Uthman and Kathir ibn Ubayd narrated to us, both saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Zuhri narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Banu Bayadah to marry Abu Hind to a woman from among them. They said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Shall we marry our daughters to our mawali?' [[One of the meanings of mawla is slave.]] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'We have created you from a male and a female and made you into peoples' – the verse." Al-Zuhri said: It was revealed concerning Abu Hind specifically. It is also said that it was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. And concerning the man to whom room was not made, [who was described as] "the son of so-and-so," the Prophet ﷺ said: [Who is the one who mentions so-and-so?] Thabit said: "I am, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said: [Look at the faces of the people.] So he looked, and he said: [What did you see?] He said: "I saw white, black and red." He said: [You do not excel them except by piety.] So this verse was revealed concerning Thabit. And concerning the man to whom room was not made, [the verse] was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when it is said to you, "Make room in the assemblies"﴾ [[Verse 11 of surah al-Mujadilah.]] [al-Mujadilah: 11] – the verse. Ibn Abbas said: On the day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ commanded Bilal, so he climbed onto the roof of the Ka'bah and called the adhan. Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-'Is said: "Praise be to Allah who took my father before he would see this day." Al-Harith ibn Hisham said: "Did Muhammad find no one other than this black crow to be a muezzin?" Suhayl ibn Amr said: "If Allah wills something, He will change it." Abu Sufyan said: "I will not say anything, for I fear that the Lord of the heavens will be informed of it." Then Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what they had said. He summoned them and asked them about what they had said, and they admitted it. So Allah revealed this verse. He rebuked them for boasting about lineages, for competing in wealth, and for disdaining the poor, for the criterion rests on piety. That is, all are from Adam and Hawwa'; excellence is only by piety. In al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon in Makkah and said: [O people, indeed Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyyah and its boasting in ancestors. People are of two kinds: a righteous, pious person who is noble before Allah, and a wicked, miserable person who is contemptible before Allah. The people are the children of Adam, and Allah created Adam from dust. Allah, Exalted is He, said: "O mankind, We have created you from a male and a female and made you into peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted."] He narrated it from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, father of Ali ibn al-Madini, and he is weak; Yahya ibn Ma'in and others declared him weak. Al-Tabari also narrated it in the book [Adab al-Nufus]: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Sa'id al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, who said: "Someone who witnessed it narrated to me, or narrated to us: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon at Mina in the middle of the days of Tashriq while he was on a camel, and he said: [O people, indeed your Lord is One, and indeed your father is One. Unquestionably, there is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a non-Arab over an Arab, nor of a black person over a red person, nor of a red person over a black person, except by piety. Have I not conveyed [the message]?" They said, "Yes." He said: "Let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent."] And in it, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: [Indeed Allah does not look at your lineages, nor at your ancestry, nor at your bodies, nor at your wealth, but He looks at your hearts. Whoever has a sound heart, Allah will show compassion to him. You are only children of Adam, and the most beloved of you to Him is the most pious of you.] And from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, on this theme, from his well-known poetry:

People, from the standpoint of origin, are equals;
their father is Adam, and their mother is Hawwa'.
A soul like a soul, and spirits alike,
and bones and limbs were created in them.
If they have some lineage from their origin
in which they boast, then it is clay and water.
Excellence belongs only to the people of knowledge,
for they are guides to the guidance for whoever seeks guidance.
The worth of each person is what he excels in,
and men are marked by their deeds.
The opposite of each person is what he is ignorant of,
and the ignorant are enemies of the people of knowledge.

The second: Allah, Exalted is He, has made clear in this verse that He created creation from male and female, and likewise at the beginning of surah al-Nisa' [[See vol. 5, p. 1 onwards.]]. Had He willed, He could have created [a human] without both of them, like His creation of Adam, or without a male, like His creation of Isa, peace be upon him, or without a female, like His creation of Hawwa' from one of the two sides. This is possible in His power, but it did not occur. It has been reported that Allah created Hawwa' from Adam, from a rib He took from his ribs, so perhaps this is that category. Ibn al-Arabi said this.

The third: Allah created creation between male and female as lineages, in-law relations, tribes and peoples. He created recognition among them through these, and made connection among them through these, for the wisdom He decreed, and He knows it best. So each person possesses his lineage, and if a man denies it, he is liable to the prescribed punishment (hadd) for slander (qadhf), such as denying it to disown his kin and his ancestry, by saying to an Arab: "O non-Arab!" and to a non-Arab: "O Arab!", and similar things by which denial actually occurs. End.

The fourth: Some of the early scholars held that the embryo comes only from the man's water, and is nurtured in the mother's womb, drawing nourishment from the blood that is in it. They argued with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised water? Then We placed it in a firm receptacle﴾ [[Verses 20, 21 of surah al-Mursalat.]] [al-Mursalat: 21]. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then He made his offspring from an extract of despised water﴾ [al-Sajdah: 8]. And His saying: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ [[Verse 37 of surah al-Qiyamah.]] [al-Qiyamah: 37]. This indicates that creation is from one water. The correct view is that creation comes only from the water of the man and the woman, because of this verse, for it is a text that does not admit of interpretation. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He was created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the loins and the ribs﴾ [[Verses 6, 7 of surah al-Tariq.]] [al-Tariq: 6]. What is meant by it is the loins of men and the ribs of women, as will be explained. As for what they argued with, there is nothing in it beyond that Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned the creation of man from water, from an extract, and from a drop, and did not attribute it to one of the two parents to the exclusion of the other. This indicates that the water, the extract and the drop belong to both of them, by the indication of what we have mentioned. And [it is also supported] by the fact that the woman emits [fluid] just as the man emits, and from this resemblance arises, as previously explained at the end of surah al-Shura [[See p. 50 of this volume.]]. And He said concerning the story of Nuh: ﴿So the waters met for a matter that had been decreed﴾ [[Verse 12 of surah al-Qamar.]] [al-Qamar: 12]. He meant the water of the sky and the water of the earth, because meeting only occurs between two. So there is no objection to the view that ﴿Then He made his offspring from an extract of despised water﴾ [al-Sajdah: 8], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised water?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 21], refers to two waters. And Allah knows best.

The fifth: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We made you into peoples and tribes that you may know one another﴾. The shu'ub (peoples) are the heads of the tribes, such as Rabi'ah, Mudar, al-Aws and al-Khazraj. Its singular is sha'b, with a fatha on the shin. They were so named because of their dispersion (tasha'ub) and their gathering, like the branches of a tree (sha'b). Sha'b is one of the words with opposite meanings: one says sha'abtuhu when one gathers it, and from this comes al-mish'ab (with a kasrah on the mim), which is the awl, because it is used to gather and to pierce. He said:

So he falls upon the noble brow, and pierces
with a horn like the tip of an awl.

[[His saying: "fakaab 'ala hurr al-jabin" means he fell on his face. "Al-madriyah" means the horn; it is also called al-mudri and al-midrah, and the plural is madar and madari. "Dhaluq" of everything means its point. "Mish'ab" means something pierced.]]

And "sha'abtahu" when you separate it, and from this the death (al-maniyyah) was called sha'ub because it separates. As for al-shi'b (with a kasrah), it is the path in the mountain, and its plural is al-shi'ab. Al-Jawhari said: al-shi'b is what branches off from the tribes of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and its plural is al-shu'ub. And al-Shu'ubiyyah is a sect that does not prefer the Arabs over the non-Arabs. As for what is in the hadith that a man from the shu'ub embraced Islam [[The complete hadith as in Lisan al-Arab: "Jizyah used to be taken from him, so Umar ordered that it should not be taken from him."]], he means from the non-Arabs. And al-sha'b is the great tribe, and it is the father of the tribes to whom they are attributed, that is, it gathers them and unites them. Ibn Abbas said: al-shu'ub are the multitude [[This saying is attributed to Ibn Jubayr. What is reported from Ibn Abbas is that "al-shu'ub" means al-jima'; and al-jima' (with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim) is the gathering point of the origin of everything, meaning the source of lineage and the origin of birth. It has also been said that it means the various divisions of people.]], like Mudar. And the qaba'il are the clans (afkhadh). Mujahid said: the shu'ub are the distant lineages, and the qaba'il are less distant than that. And he also said that the shu'ub are the nearer lineage. Qatadah said the same. Al-Mahdawi reported the first from him, and al-Mawardi the second. The poet said:

I saw the Sa'ud from many peoples,
but I did not see anyone like Sa'd ibn Malik.

Another said:

Tribes from peoples, among whom there is
no noble one who is counted, nor any well-born one.

It has been said: the shu'ub are the Arabs of Yemen from Qahtan, and the qaba'il are from Rabi'ah, Mudar and the rest of Adnan. It has also been said: the shu'ub are the clans of the non-Arabs, and the qaba'il are the clans of the Arabs. Ibn Abbas, in one narration, said: the shu'ub are the mawali, and the qaba'il are the Arabs. Al-Qushayri said: according to this, the shu'ub are those whose origin of lineage is unknown, such as the Hind, the Jabal [[al-jabal: a nation of created beings and a group of people; it has many dialects. See vol. 15, p. 47 of this commentary.]], and the Turks, while the qaba'il are from among the Arabs. Al-Mawardi: It is possible that the shu'ub are those attributed to regions and valleys, and the qaba'il are those who share lineages. The poet said:

They scattered into peoples, so every island
has in it an Amir al-Mu'minin and a pulpit.

Abu Ubayd related from Ibn al-Kalbi, from his father: the sha'b is larger than the qabilah, then the fasilah, then the 'imarah, then the batn, then the fakhidh. It has also been said: the sha'b, then the qabilah, then the 'imarah, then the batn, then the fakhidh, then the fasilah, then the 'ashirah. Some men of letters versified this, saying:

Aim for the sha'b, for it is the greatest living group
in number among the Hawa', then the qabilah.
Then follow it the 'imarah, then the
batn and the fakhidh after it, and the fasilah.
Then after them the 'ashirah, but
compared to what we have mentioned, it is little.

Another said:

A qabilah, before it a sha'b, and after them both
an 'imarah, then a batn following it, then a fakhidh.
A young man is only sheltered by his fasilah,
and there is no mending for an arrow that has no feathers.
[[al-qadhadh (plural of qadhah): the feathers of an arrow.]]

Sixth: His saying, Exalted is He, "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you" (inna akramakum 'inda Allahi atqakum). This has already been discussed in Surah al-Zukhruf at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44] (see p. 93 of this part).[[See p. 93 of this part.]] In this verse there is an indication that taqwa (God-consciousness) is what is regarded before Allah, Exalted is He, and before His Messenger, rather than lineage and ancestry. It has also been read as "anna" with a fatha. It is as if it were asked: why should one not boast of lineages? It is answered: because "the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you," not the most closely related of you.

In al-Tirmidhi, from Samurah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Ancestry (hasab) is wealth, and nobility (karam) is taqwa." He said: "This is a hadith that is hasan, gharib, sahih." This goes back to His saying, Exalted is He: "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." It has also come explicitly from him, peace be upon him: "Whoever wishes to be the most noble of people, let him fear Allah." Taqwa means observing the limits of Allah, Exalted is He, in commands and prohibitions, adopting the qualities He has commanded you to adopt, and keeping away from what He has forbidden you. This has passed in more than one place.

And in a report from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, Exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'I created lineage, and you created lineages. I made the most noble of you the most righteous of you, but you refused except to say, "So-and-so son of so-and-so." Today I raise up My lineage and lower your lineages. Where are the righteous? Where are the righteous?'" Al-Tabari related from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, My friends (awliya') on the Day of Resurrection are the righteous, even if a lineage is closer than another lineage. People will come with deeds, and you will come with the world, carrying it upon your necks, saying, 'O Muhammad!' and I will say, 'Thus and thus,'" and he turned aside, to each side [of himself].

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ openly, not secretly, say: "The family of Abu (Ali ibn Abi Talib?) are not my friends (awliya'); my friend is only Allah and the righteous believers." And from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ was asked: "Who is the most noble of people?" He said: "Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then the most noble of them in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "About the mines of the Arabs? The best of them in the Jahiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, when they gain understanding." And they recited verses on this:

What does the servant do with the might of wealth,
when all might belongs to the one who is God-fearing?
Whoever knows Allah, and the knowledge of Allah does not annihilate him,
that one is the wretched.

Seventh: al-Tabari mentioned: "Told me[[In the manuscripts H and N: "Amr".]] 'Umar ibn Muhammad, who said: Ubayd ibn Ishaq al-Attar told us, who said: Mandal ibn 'Ali told us, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: A man of the Ansar married a woman, and her lineage was criticized. The man said: "I did not marry her for her lineage; I married her for her religion and her character." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Does it harm you that you are not of the family of Hajib[[A chief of the Arab chiefs in the Jahiliyyah. He lived to see Islam and embraced it.]] ibn Zurarah?" Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted is He, brought Islam, and by it He raised the lowly, completed the deficient, and removed reproach; so there is no reproach upon a Muslim. Reproach is only the reproach of the Jahiliyyah." The Prophet ﷺ also said: "Indeed I hope to be the most fearful of you of Allah and the most knowing of you of what I guard against." For this reason he was the most noble of mankind before Allah, Exalted is He. Ibn al-'Arabi said: This is what Malik considered regarding equality (kafa'ah) in marriage. Abdullah related from Malik: a mawla may marry an Arab woman, and he argued from this verse. Abu Hanifah and al-Shafi'i said: lineage and wealth are taken into account.

In the Sahih, from 'A'ishah, that Abu Hudhayfah ibn 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, who was among those who witnessed Badr with the Prophet ﷺ, adopted Salim and married him to Hind[[Also called Fatimah.]] the daughter of his brother al-Walid ibn 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, while he was a mawla of a woman of the Ansar. Dubaa'ah bint al-Zubayr was under al-Miqdad[[His father's name was Amr ibn Tha'labah; he was adopted by al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, and he was one of the seven who were the first to openly profess Islam.]] ibn al-Aswad.

I say: The sister of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf was under Bilal, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was under Zayd ibn Harithah. This indicates the permissibility of marrying Arab women to mawali, and equality is only considered in religion.

Also evidence for this is what Sahl ibn Sa'd related in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, that a man passed by the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "What do you say about this one?" They said: "He is worthy, if he proposes, that he be married; and if he intercedes, that his intercession be accepted; and if he speaks, that he be listened to." He fell silent. Then a man from the poor Muslims passed by, and he said: "What do you say about this one?" They said: "He is worthy, if he proposes, that he not be married; and if he intercedes, that his intercession not be accepted; and if he speaks, that he not be listened to." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This one is better than a world full of the like of this one."

He ﷺ also said: "A woman is married for her wealth, her beauty, and her religion" (and in another narration: "and her lineage"). "So choose the one with religion; may your hands be rubbed with dust (tariba yadaka)." Salman proposed his daughter to Abu Bakr, and he accepted; he proposed his daughter to 'Umar, and he hesitated; then he asked Salman to marry her, but Salman did not. Bilal proposed to the daughter of al-Bukayr, but her brothers refused, and they harmed him. Bilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, what I have suffered from the sons of al-Bukayr! I proposed to their sister, and they refused me and harmed me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry because of the matter. The news reached them, and they came to their sister and said: "What have we suffered because of you?" Their sister said: "My affair is in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So they married her off.

The Prophet ﷺ said about Abu Hind when he cupped him: "Marry Abu Hind, and marry into his family." He was a mawla of Bani Bayadah. Al-Daraqutni related from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that Abu Hind, a mawla of Bani Bayadah, was a cupper, and he cupped the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is pleased to look at one whom Allah has shaped faith in his heart, let him look at Abu Hind." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Marry him, and marry into him."

Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: Lineage may also be taken into account in equality in marriage, namely connection to the tree of prophethood, or to the scholars who are the heirs of the prophets, or to those esteemed for asceticism and righteousness. But a pious believer is better than a corrupt person of noble lineage. If the two are equally pious, then the one of noble lineage among them is given precedence, just as a young man is given precedence over an old man in prayer when they are equal in piety.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on Surah 49, verse 14:**

It was revealed concerning some Bedouin (a'rab) of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzayma. They came to the Messenger of God ﷺ in a year of drought, and they professed the two testimonies (ash-shahadatayn), but they were not believers in their hearts. They also spoiled the roads of Madinah with excrement and raised its prices. They used to say to the Messenger of God ﷺ, "We have come to you with our burdens and our dependents, and we did not fight you as the Banu so-and-so fought you, so give us from the charity," and they began to press favours upon him. So God the Exalted revealed this verse concerning them.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Bedouin who wished to call themselves by the name of the emigration (hijra) before they had emigrated. So God informed them that their name is the name of the Bedouin, not the name of the Emigrants (Muhajirun).

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the Bedouin mentioned in Surat al-Fath: the Bedouin of Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam, Ghifar, al-Dil and Ashja'. They said, "We believe," so that they would be safe for their own selves and their property. Then, when they were called to go forth to Madinah, they stayed behind, and so it was revealed.

In summary, the verse is specific to some of the Bedouin, because among them are those who believe in God and the Last Day, as God the Exalted has described.

The meaning of ﴿But say, "We have submitted"﴾ is: they surrendered (istaslamna) out of fear of killing and captivity. Is this the attribute of the hypocrites?

Because they submitted outwardly while their hearts had not believed. The reality of faith (iman) is affirmation (tasdiq) in the heart, whereas submission (islam) is acceptance of what the Prophet ﷺ brought, outwardly, and that preserves blood. ﴿And if you obey God and His Messenger﴾ means: if you sincerely hold to faith. ﴿He will not deprive you (la yalitkum) of anything of your deeds﴾, that is, He will not diminish for you anything. Lata yalituhu means: he diminished it, from the verb *lata* (to reduce).

Abu 'Amr read *la ya'litkum* with a hamza, from *alta* (*yalit*, *altan*), and this is the choice of Abu Hatim, on the basis of the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿And We did not diminish anything of their deeds﴾ [52:21]. A poet said:

*Convey from me to the Banu Tha'l a message, delivered in full, neither diminished nor false.*

Abu 'Ubayd preferred the first reading. Ru'ba said:

*And a night of dew I travelled, and no lion turned me back from its journey.*

That is, no obstacle prevented me from its journey. Likewise *alatahu 'an wajhihi* (he turned him away from his purpose): *fa'ala* and *af'ala* have the same meaning. It is also said: *ma alatahu min 'amalihi shay'an*, meaning: it did not diminish his deed at all, like *altahu*, as al-Farra' said. He recited:

*And they eat what the rain-bearer (al-waliyy) nourished, and it did not diminish; as if on the edges of the rivulets are the fields.*

Al-Qurtubi's statement: *fa-lam yalit* means he did not diminish anything of it. *A'natha* means "caused to grow", as one says: *ma a'natha al-ardu shay'an*, meaning the earth did not produce anything. *Al-waliyy* is the rain that falls after the first spring rain (al-wasmi), the first spring rain being so named because it marks (yasim) the earth with vegetation. It was called *waliyy* because it follows (yali) the wasmi.

He did not say *la ya'litakum* (in the dual) because obedience to God the Exalted is obedience to the Messenger.

Allah the Exalted said: "The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and then have not doubted" (lam yartabu), meaning they affirmed and did not waver, and they proved this through jihad and righteous deeds. "Those are the truthful ones" in their faith, not those who embraced Islam out of fear of being killed or hope for gain.

When this was revealed, the Bedouins (al-A'rab) swore that they were believers both in secret and in public, and they were lying, so the following was revealed: "Say: Would you inform Allah about your religion? And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things."

Allah the Exalted said: "The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and then have not doubted" (lam yartabu), meaning they affirmed and did not waver, and they proved this through jihad and righteous deeds. "Those are the truthful ones" in their faith, not those who embraced Islam out of fear of being killed or hope for gain.

When this was revealed, the Bedouins (al-A'rab) swore that they were believers both in secret and in public, and they were lying, so the following was revealed: "Say: Would you inform Allah about your religion? And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 49, verse 17–18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam.﴾ This refers to their saying: "We have come to you with our burdens and our dependents."

The "an" (that) is in the position of the accusative, with the implied sense of li-an aslamu (because they embraced Islam). Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favour to me," i.e., by your Islam. ﴿Rather, God bestows a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith.﴾ The "an" is in the accusative position, its implied sense being bi-an (by virtue of that). It is also said: li-anna (because). In the codex of Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "idha hadakum" (when He guided you). ﴿If you are truthful [that you are believers].﴾

ʿĀṣim recited "in hadakum" with a kasra, but this is remote, because of His saying: "if you are truthful." It is not said: "He bestows a favour upon you that He guide you, if you are truthful." The apparent recitation is "an hadakum." This does not indicate that they were believers, because the implied meaning of the statement is: "If you believe, then that is a favour of God upon you." ﴿Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and God is seeing of what you do.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr recited it with the ya' (third person), as a report, in reply to His saying: "the Bedouins say." The rest recited it with the ta' (second person), as direct address.

Found in manuscript "z" the following: "And God knows best what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final abode, and there is no power and no strength except with God, the Most High, the Mighty, and He is sufficient for me and the best Disposer of affairs."

4 Muharram 1385 / 5 May 1965

Edited by Ahmad Abd al-'Alim al-Bardouni

Then, by the help of God Most High, the sixteenth part of the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi, followed, God willing, by the seventeenth part, beginning with:

"Surat (Qaf)," the seventeenth part.
